sections.name: CTA band
sections.description: The closing ask: a rounded brand-gradient panel that bookends the page with the hero promise, ink primary CTA plus ghost secondary, or a slim justified band with one headline and one button. Place it last on any page that must convert.

usedBy.note: Scheduling form embedded directly in the band, not a link out
Closing band repeats the hero headline verbatim: bookend effect
Choice-of-demo: self-guided tour vs video vs live, instead of one button
Closer as a 3-card journey: Book demo / Implement / Drive outcomes
Copyable code snippet as the second CTA path for developers
Brand-metaphor close sustaining the hero promise

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Short uppercase kicker above the headline; empty string hides it

props.name: sub
props.doc: Supporting line; empty string hides it (the justified variant drops it)

props.name: ctaLabel
props.doc: Primary action label

props.name: secondaryCtaLabel
props.doc: Secondary action label; empty string renders a single-CTA band

props.name: layout
props.doc: gradient-panel = centered rounded brand-gradient panel (the section's one gradient element); justified = slim full-width band, headline start, CTA end

props.headline: Your competitors are making faster decisions. Are you?

sections.name: Newsletter capture
sections.description: Single-field email capture for editorial surfaces, framed as access to the weekly brief rather than a subscription. Three placements: centered block, split band card, and a compact strip that sits just above the footer. Submit swaps to an inline confirmation.

usedBy.note: Newsletter capture merged into the final CTA band
Minimal email capture just above the footer

props.name: sub
props.doc: Shown in the centered and band layouts; the footer-embed strip shows privacyNote instead

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Email input placeholder

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Replaces the form after submit

props.name: layout
props.doc: centered = standalone block; band = two-column card; footer-embed = compact strip above the footer

sections.name: Lead capture split form
sections.description: Two-column capture for high-intent asks: benefit copy and proof bullets on one side, a sticky card form (name, email, company, team size, free-text ask) on the other. The whats-inside variant boxes the bullets as gated-asset contents under a titled panel.

usedBy.note: Inline signup embedded mid-homepage, not just a header CTA
Demo form lets the prospect choose what to preview

props.name: bullets
props.doc: Checklist of what the prospect gets; empty array hides the block

props.name: bulletsTitle
props.doc: Uppercase title over the bullets, shown only in the whats-inside layout

props.name: items
props.doc: Form fields; type is 'text' | 'email' | 'select' | 'textarea' | 'multiselect'

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Replaces the form card contents after submit

props.name: layout
props.doc: standard = bullets as a plain checklist; whats-inside = bullets boxed in a titled sunken panel

sections.name: Multi-step form
sections.description: A three-step progressive form in one card: contact details, a stack picker with toggle chips, then the first question, with a segmented progress bar, step counter and back/next controls. Use when one long form would scare off a cold visitor.

props.name: steps
props.type: Array<{title, fields: Array<{label, type, placeholder?, options?}>}>
props.doc: Ordered steps; field type is 'text' | 'email' | 'textarea' | 'multiselect'

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Primary button label on the final step

props.name: progressLabel
props.doc: Counter template; {current} and {total} are replaced, e.g. 'Step 2 of 3'

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: Replaces the card contents after submit

sections.name: ROI calculator
sections.description: Interactive ROI math as a mid-page conversion tool: three sliders (team size, weekly hours, hourly cost) drive live monthly-value, hours-reclaimed and payback-days figures in a results card, with the automation assumption stated in plain sight. For pricing and landing pages.

usedBy.note: Inline ROI calculator as a mid-page conversion tool
Cost estimator paired with an ROI calculator on the pricing page

props.name: teamLabel
props.doc: Label for the team-size slider (1 to 50 people)

props.name: hoursLabel
props.doc: Label for the weekly-hours slider (1 to 20 hours)

props.name: rateLabel
props.doc: Label for the hourly-cost slider ($30 to $250)

props.name: defaultTeam
props.doc: Initial team-size value

props.name: defaultHours
props.doc: Initial hours-per-week value

props.name: defaultRate
props.doc: Initial loaded hourly cost in dollars

props.name: automationShare
props.doc: Share of reporting time Alfred absorbs, 0 to 1; drives all three outputs

props.name: planPrice
props.doc: Monthly plan price in dollars used for the payback-days figure

props.name: planNote
props.doc: Caption under the payback figure naming the plan

props.name: assumption
props.doc: The stated assumption behind the math, in Alfred's voice
